questions.prompt: G2 BRIEF — netslack (ASP.NET Core + EF Core Slack clone). Review finding A: WorkspaceService normalises the slug with its own copy of the rule for the precheck and the race-recovery query, while Workspace.Create stores the result of the domain's NormalizeSlug; and a request without `slug` throws NullReferenceException, which the middleware maps to 500 instead of 400. Delegate the fix to a coding agent. Write the brief: goal, allowed files, boundaries, test command, stop condition. Commit to your brief first, then tick the checkpoints you covered and add up the weights.

keyPoints.text: [w3] Goal: ONE normalisation function, exposed by the domain, used for the precheck, the stored value and the recovery query, so the three lookups can never disagree.
keyPoints.quote: Fix direction: expose one normalization function from the domain and use it in all three places.

keyPoints.text: [w3] Goal (second half): a create request with a missing slug answers 400 via ArgumentException, not 500; the null must reach the domain guard instead of crashing on `.Trim()` first.
[w2] Allowed files: Workspace.cs (make the normaliser reachable), WorkspaceService.cs, and tests (ScopeHarness Program.cs and/or WorkflowTests.cs).
[w3] Boundary: keep the race-recovery design — re-query persisted occupancy after DbUpdateException; never parse provider error strings or map every unique violation to a slug conflict.
[w2] Boundary: do not touch the exception middleware's mapping table; the fix is to throw the right exception, not to remap NullReferenceException.
[w2] Test command: the ScopeHarness run with shared compilation off, because the native test project targets .NET 8 and did not run on the .NET 10-only machine.

[w2] Stop condition: all harness cases pass plus a new case for the missing-slug 400 path and one proving the precheck uses the stored form; stop and report if the native suite cannot run instead of claiming it passed.

questions.prompt: G2 PRE-MORTEM — same delegation. What will an agent most likely get wrong here, and which line of your brief prevents it?

keyPoints.text: [w3] It 'simplifies' recovery by catching DbUpdateException and always returning Conflict, which turns unrelated persistence failures into fake duplicates.
[w2] It fixes the 500 by adding NullReferenceException to the middleware switch, hiding real null bugs everywhere else.
[w2] It changes the normalisation rule itself (e.g. collapsing repeated dashes) in the same diff, which changes which existing slugs collide.
keyPoints.quote: If either copy changes (say, collapsing repeated dashes), the precheck and recovery query look up a different key from the one that is stored

keyPoints.text: [w2] It drops or rewrites the unique index, losing the only real guard against two concurrent creates.
[w1] It reports `dotnet test` as green on a machine where the .NET 8 test target cannot even restore.

questions.prompt: G2 HANDBACK REVIEW — the agent hands back a diff and a green run. What do you check before accepting it?

keyPoints.text: [w3] Exactly one normalisation implementation remains; the service's inline Trim/ToLowerInvariant/Replace chain is gone.
[w3] The five original harness cases still pass, including 'unrelated persistence failure is not swallowed'.
[w2] The pasted output names which runner actually executed (harness vs native) and the .NET version, matching what the verification record says is possible.
[w2] A missing-slug request is shown to produce 400 with the domain's message, not a 500 problem document.
[w1] The handback lists the unrelated review findings it saw (AsNoTracking myth, dead Location route) as follow-ups instead of fixing them in this diff.
keyPoints.quote: The `Location` header names a route that does not exist.
